target.title: RFC: TapesClaw for Claw telemetry storage and querying
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This RFC proposes bundling a first party agent telemetry store for Claw LLM turns, sessions, and metadata in order to provide enriched "evidence" for Skills Workshop skill improvements, history scans, and generally, enhance the "self improving" aspect of OpenClaw.

## Why This Change Was Made

Had a number of great chats with @Patrick-Erichsen re: how OpenClaw and the skills capabilities could benefit from enhanced prescience into exactly _"what"_ and _"how"_ a Claw did something. [`tapes` is an open source agent telemetry system](https://github.com/papercomputeco/tapes) we've developed that does exactly that: ingests LLM inference trace telemetry and provides the queryability to mine past context.

This proposes introducing a `tapesclaw` plugin that utilizes this functionality and a new `skills_workshop.evidence` (with other lifecycle hooks for mining evidence supported in the future) that can be used to query for relevant durable session data from past LLM turns.

## User Impact

By default, `tapes` and `tapesclaw` would be bundled with installs of OpenClaw. Users who want to opt out can disable during install. And LLM inference turns would never be blocked on ingesting or querying for data.

Users who utilize the Skills Workshop and the `/learn` step would then see better skills in the `PROPOSAL.md` stage as the agent Workshop will have used real evidence from `tapes` and the `tapesclaw` plugin.
